strandz

site

Build

Pages are written in Markdown and converted to HTML by build.js.

npm install
npm run build

The generated site goes to dist/, keeping the source directory structure. index.md (or INDEX.md) becomes index.html, and links between .md files are rewritten to point at the generated .html pages.

Page metadata

Pages can set metadata in YAML front matter. It is removed from the rendered Markdown and used to fill the HTML <head>:

---
title: Projects
description: An index of projects, grouped by category.
author: Danny Ayers
lang: en
canonical: https://strandz.it/
ogType: website
keywords:
  - projects
  - audio
---

# Projects

Supported fields: title, description, author, lang, keywords, tags, canonical, image, ogType, siteName, robots, noindex, date, and draft. Set draft: true to leave a page out of the build. If title is absent, the first # heading is used, falling back to the filename.

To write the HTML next to the Markdown sources instead:

npm run build:in-place

To choose another output directory:

node build.js --out <dir>
